To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bounded difference inequality and the method of empirical processes can be extended from bounded variables to sub-Gaussian and/or sub-exponential variables.

the bounded difference inequality holds for sub-Gaussian and for sub-exponential random variables and that this implies uniform convergence results for linear regression and principal component analysis for potentially unbounded input and output variables.

(i) the sub-Gaussian condition is a natural generalization of the bounded difference condition, (ii) the sub-exponential condition is a natural extension of the sub-Gaussian one, and (iii) the sub-exponentially bounded difference condition is a natural and useful generalization of the sub-exponential one.
